arguments.rule_content:
title: Suspicious Kerberos Pre-Auth Failure Followed by Success
logsource:
  category: authentication
  product: windows
  service: security
  definition: 'EventID: 4771 (failed pre-auth) and 4768/4769 (TGT/TGS success)'
detection:
  failed_preauth:
    EventID: 4771
    LogonType: 3
  successful_auth:
    EventID: 4624
    LogonType: 3
  condition: failed_preauth and successful_auth and same_source_ip and same_user
  timeframe: 5m
  same_source_ip: source_ip = failed_preauth.source_ip
  same_user: user = failed_preauth.user
level: high
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate account lockout followed by unlock and login
  - Time synchronization issues causing transient failures
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1558/004/
description: Detects potential AS-REP roasting or password guessing attacks where a failed Kerberos pre-auth is immediately followed by a successful authentication for the same user from the same host.
author: SOC_Team

arguments.summary: A low-severity port scan alert from 10.0.5.14 to 10.0.4.1 triggered initial detection. Further investigation revealed that the true source was 10.0.5.42 (WS-FIN-042), a high-criticality finance workstation. The host was compromised via a phishing email in Outlook, leading to execution of encoded PowerShell, which loaded a malicious DLL (Cobalt Strike beacon) via rundll32. The beacon established C2 communication with a known-bad IP (198.51.100.23) over HTTPS. Subsequent lateral movement attempts were detected via SMB access to 10.0.5.50 and failed Kerberos authentication to 10.0.3.10. Despite detection, containment actions (firewall block, EPP isolation) were denied due to policy misconfiguration and IAM issues.
